Customer to share 2 weeks of production traces / request logs (anonymized) (due 2027-10-01)

summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling to size Redwood Dedicated vs hosted fallback. Customer (Arcane Pay) provided high-level concurrency/QPS patterns: steady baseline ~5 QPS, peak bursts up to ~60 QPS (batch settlement windows). Success criteria: p95 latency < 300ms for short responses, correctness/regression parity with current on-prem model, and cost per 1M tokens within their budgeted threshold. Action items: share traces, Redwood to run benchmark harness, schedule deep-dive after run.
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-09-27
- Time: 15:00 - 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~60 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Arcane Pay Head of ML), Oliver Grant (Arcane Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (CTO)

Topics: workload characterization, qps/concurrency, input/output token distribution, latency SLOs, benchmark plan, timeline, security/compliance checks

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros \u000b\u000b\u000b i'm sofia, AE on the account. ravi from our solutions team is here.
[00:08] Maya: hi, maya \u000b\u000b\u000b yea thanks. we want to scope a p-o-c to run your inference across a subset of our payment pipelines.
[00:14] Ravi: cool, can you give us a bit of context \u000b\u000b\u000b production traffic shape, what triggers bursts, and what success looks like for you?
[00:22] Oliver: sure \u000b\u000b\u000b so our system handles transaction enrichment and fraud scoring. normal weekdays baseline is roughly 4-6 qps for the ML scoring endpoint, but we have batch settlement windows at 02:00 UTC where qps spikes up to 50-60 qps for about 15 minutes.
[00:36] Lena: to add, most requests are small \u000b\u000b\u000b like 1-2 short fields to enrich; we call the LLM for intent extraction and merchant risk summarization.
[00:46] Sofia: good, and what about concurrency \u000b\u000b\u000b how many parallel requests do you see?
[00:51] Maya: steady concurrency usually 6-8, peaks up to 24-30 during the 15-minute windows. sometimes we also have backfills where we run hundreds in parallel but those are queued batch jobs.
[01:05] Ravi: do you have token distributions? avg input and output tokens?
[01:09] Maya: yeah, we estimated avg input ~45 tokens, output ~110 tokens. 80% of calls are under 200 output tokens. occasional long reports upto 800 tokens but that's <1% of traffic.
[01:22] Sofia: ok great. success metrics? latency p95 targets? accuracy/regression?
[01:27] Lena: p95 under 300ms for the common short path would be ideal but we realize that's tight \u000b\u000b\u000b p95 under 500ms would be acceptable if cost is reasonable. correctness \u000b\u000b\u000b we need parity with our current on-prem model; we'll have a QA eval suite.
[01:41] Ravi: from an infra standpoint, any VPC/on-prem constraints?
[01:45] Oliver: we prefer private deployment for PCI adjacency but open to Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering. we require KMS integration and audit logs retention for 90 days.
[01:56] Sofia: noted, we'll include KMS & audit in the SOW. any regulatory needs \u000b\u000b\u000b SOC2 / ISO?
[02:02] Maya: SOC2 Type II is required for production workloads.
[02:06] Ravi: great. one thing we usually model is the token cost vs latency tradeoff \u000b\u000b\u000b given your input/output distribution, we can estimate per-1M token cost for hosted and dedicated. we'll run bench to measure actual p95 and throughput.
[02:20] Oliver: how do you handle KV cache & prefix caching? we have a lot of repeated prefixes for merchant descriptors.
[02:26] Ravi: our runtime supports prefix/KV cache \u000b\u000b\u000b though sorry sometimes the transcripts say K-V cash, but it's KV cache \u000b\u000b\u000b it helps a lot for repeated tokens; it reduces extra compute and latency.
[02:36] Maya: what size instance do you recommend for a start?
[02:39] Ravi: based on those numbers \u000b\u000b\u000b baseline 5 qps, peaks 60 qps for 15 min, concurrency up to 30 \u000b\u000b\u000b i'd model a Dedicated pool of 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale for burst capacity OR 1 larger GPU with aggressive batching. for conservative POC, 2 cards gives headroom for the burst windows.
[02:59] Sofia: and cost ballpark?
[03:01] Ravi: i'll put numbers in the SOW, but rough order \u000b\u000b\u000b Dedicated monthly commit for that size typically in the mid 10s of thousands USD; hosted pay-as-you-go will show higher per-token cost but no commit.
[03:12] Lena: we need exact numbers to go back to procurement \u000b\u000b\u000b please include a run-rate for 1M, 5M, 10M tokens.
[03:19] Sofia: will do.
[03:21] Ravi: for benches, we propose the following plan: 1) customer shares 2 weeks of anonymized traces and token distribution; 2) Redwood engineers run a synthetic replay at target QPS and peak patterns against the candidate model variants; 3) capture p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, and token cost; 4) review results and iterate.
[03:38] Maya: timeline?
[03:40] Ravi: once we have traces, we can schedule a 2-day run \u000b\u000b\u000b prep + 1 full-day of synthetic testing \u000b\u000b\u000b aiming for the benchmark run the week of 2027-10-05.
[03:51] Oliver: for synthetic tests, can you simulate our bursting windows pattern? we need the 15-minute high qps replicated.
[03:56] Ravi: yes \u000b\u000b\u000b our harness can replay time-based patterns and ramp up. we'll also test caching on/off to show cost differences.
[04:05] Maya: what about quantization \u000b\u000b\u000b are you recommending quantized model to save cost?
[04:09] Ravi: we support quantization-friendly execution paths; often for retrieval/short outputs int8/4 quant variants reduce cost with marginal quality loss. we'll run evals against your QA set to check regressions.
[04:20] Lena: SSO and SAML for console?
[04:23] Sofia: yes, Redwood Console supports SAML/SSO and RBAC; include that in the SOW.
[04:29] Maya: any gotchas with latency for low-token responses when using batching?
[04:33] Ravi: batching helps throughput but can add tail latency. we use continuous batching and latency SLOs \u000b\u000b\u000b for low-latency paths we'll set a max batch wait threshold to keep p95 in range. it's a configuration knob.
[04:46] Sofia: ok, let's talk numbers to include in the POC sizing doc. can you confirm the numbers one more time? qps baseline ~5, peak bursts to ~60 qps for 15 minutes, steady concurrency 6-8, peak concurrency 24-30, avg input 45 tokens, avg output 110 tokens, 1% long tails up to 800 tokens.
[05:06] Maya: yes that's accurate.
[05:09] Ravi: given that, here's a quick back-of-envelope: with avg 155 tokens per call (input+output) * 5 qps steady => ~775 tokens/sec => ~2.8M tokens/hour steady. For peak 60 qps, that's ~9.3k tokens/sec, or ~33M tokens/hour during the 15-minute window. Those bursts blow up hourly totals if frequent.
[05:33] Oliver: that helps. our cost model needs to account for burst windows and whether caching will drop effective tokens.
[05:40] Sofia: for the POC we'll measure three configurations: hosted (no commit), Dedicated small (2 x A100 equiv) with caching, and Dedicated with quantized model. we'll compare p95, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:56] Maya: prefer dedicated if price/perf is good and compliance checks pass.
[06:01] Ravi: note on security \u000b\u000b\u000b we'll provide SOC2 cert, KMS integration docs, and audit log capabilities. I'll attach the security pack in the SOW.
[06:10] Lena: fine. on benchmarks \u000b\u000b\u000b how do you measure correctness? we have an eval set with pass/fail criteria.
[06:15] Ravi: we'll run your eval set against candidate model variants (baseline on-prem model, open model we propose). we'll report precision/recall and any regressions. we can run automatic diff tests on outputs; if there's any regression we flag and discuss tradeoffs.
[06:30] Sofia: any legal / procurement constraints we should know now?
[06:34] Oliver: standard. procurement will need SLAs and data residency notes \u000b\u000b\u000b we're US-first for now.
[06:39] Sofia: noted.
[06:41] Maya: one more question \u000b\u000b\u000b for the POC, do you need full payloads or can we mask PII?
[06:46] Ravi: masking is fine \u000b\u000b\u000b we only need tokenized traces that reflect real token distribution; redwood doesn't need raw PII.
[06:52] Sofia: okay great. final recap and next steps?
[06:55] Sofia: action items recap: sofia to send SOW & pricing, ravi to prepare benchmark harness and load scripts, maya to send traces and token distributions, oliver to provide network constraints. timeline target: bench run week of 10/05, deep dive w/results 10/07.
[07:12] Maya: sounds good. we'll try to get the traces by Friday.
[07:15] Lena: thanks everyone.
[07:17] Sofia: thanks \u000b\u000b\u000b we'll follow up in email with attachments (SOW link, security pack). links: SOW draft (internal link) https://redwood.example/sow/arcane-pay, security pack: https://redwood.example/security-pack

Notes / imperfect transcriptions: some words like "K V cash" appear instead of KV cache; product names sometimes truncated (Redood Dedicated). natural filler and cross-talk present.

Bench plan summary (text captured in call):
- Data needed: 2 weeks anonymized traces, token distribution, example payloads (masked)
- Synthetic harness: replay baseline and burst windows, measure p50/p95, GPU util, token cost
- Configs to test: hosted API, Dedicated 2x A100-eq, Dedicated + quantized model
- Success criteria: p95 latency <300ms for short path OR <500ms acceptable; no functional regression on eval suite; cost per 1M tokens within procurement threshold

End of transcript.
